newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania expects 1997 wheat crop of 6.0 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Romania expects 1997 wheat crop of 6.0 mln tonnes.

text.p: Romania's Agriculture Ministry said on Friday it expected a wheat crop of around 6.0 million tonnes next year as farmers increase the sown area to more than 2.0 million hectares.
It rejected media reports that the 1997 crop would be even thinner than this year's 3.1 million tonnes after farmers' failed to sow the planned area on time.

"The area sown to wheat now extends to 1.9 million hectares and with forecasts saying the weather will stay fine we have reason to believe we will have more than 2.0 million hectares under wheat in the next few days," ministry spokesman Alexandru Brad told Reuters.
He said proper farming work would put next year's per hectare average yield at around 3,000 kg.
"That means the total wheat crop next year will be of around 6.0 million tonnes," Brad said.
Romania had 2.11 million hectares under wheat for the 1996 crop. But an early and prolonged winter damaged crops on half that area, giving the country less than 60 percent of its bumper 1995 harvest.
The 1996 crop, enough only to meet domestic consumption and replenish state reserves, ruined the cash-strapped country's plans to export grain.

Senior Agriculture Ministry officials recently said Romania could even hope for as much as 7.0 million tonnes of wheat in 1997, which they said might help it re-emerge as a major player on the world grain market.
Last year Romania exported over 1.3 million tonnes from its wheat harvest of 7.8 million tonnes.
